tool_definitions.name: subagent
tool_definitions.description: start independent subagents with a shared optional system prompt and individual tasks, send one a message, which a running subagent reads once its current step finishes and a finished one takes as a follow-up, or send every running subagent the same message by leaving out the name, and inspect or control them by name, or by the alias a task gave its subagent; call models to list valid models and their supported efforts, then give every task an explicit provider/model@effort selection from that list; use provider/model when no efforts are listed; a follow-up keeps the model the subagent started on; only a limited number run at once, and start says how many are running against the limit; a subagent knows only a short description of its sandbox, your system_prompt, and its prompt: none of your instructions, context files or conversation reach it, so give it everything it needs; each subagent can read but not write its workspace, and has a shell only while you do, it can also read your configured read, home, and executable search paths, but not your configured write paths or anything granted during this session, writing only to its own scratch, which is subagents/<name> inside your scratch but which it calls /tmp, so a /tmp path it reports may mean your /tmp/subagents/<name>/...; it reads the rest of your scratch only where one of those configured paths covers it, so otherwise put what it needs in its prompt, or, for a follow-up, write files into your /tmp/subagents/<name> and refer to them by the /tmp paths it sees; never trust an answer blindly: however confident, it is an unverified claim that may be wrong, miss part of its task, or describe checks it never ran, so before you act on it or pass it on, verify what matters yourself, such as by opening files it reports, rerunning key commands, or reading the code it cites; a finished subagent's answer, and any message a running one sends you, reaches you on its own, between your tool calls while you work or by waking you once you have ended your turn, so carry on or end your turn rather than waiting or polling for it

parameters.name: names
parameters.description: the subagents for status, output, or stop, by name or alias; empty means all of them

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: the subagent to send a message to, by name or alias (for send); absent means every running subagent

parameters.name: system_prompt
parameters.description: the only instructions every subagent shares, beside a short description of its sandbox (for start)

parameters.name: subagents

item_fields.name: model
item_fields.description: the exact provider/model@effort selection from action=models; omit @effort only for a model that takes no effort

item_fields.name: prompt
item_fields.description: the whole task for this subagent, with whatever context it needs

item_fields.name: intent
item_fields.description: what this subagent is for, as a 5 to 7 word phrase opening with a capitalised -ing verb, such as "Reviewing the parser for missed errors"

item_fields.name: workspace
item_fields.description: the subagent's read-only workspace, any directory you can read outside your /tmp; absent means yours

item_fields.name: name
item_fields.description: an optional alias of your own for this subagent, unique in this session, which works anywhere its given name does

parameters.description: one task per independent subagent (for start)
